Event Planning Checklist

Whether it's a conference, a fundraiser, or a company party, every event runs on the same backbone: a clear goal, a locked budget, the right venue, and a run-of-show nobody has to guess at. This checklist gathers the tasks that make or break an event so you can delegate with confidence. Use it as-is, or open it in Gisti to assign owners, and see the rest of our event and party checklists.

verified Curated by the Gisti team · Updated July 2026

Event Planning Checklist · 18 items

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Define the event's goal and how you'll measure success

    Attendance, funds raised, or leads booked — pick the metric up front.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Set the date and hold a backup date
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Set the budget and set up a simple way to track spending against it
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Estimate the headcount and build the guest or attendee list
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Book the venue and confirm its capacity and layout
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Confirm exactly what the venue includes: tables, chairs, AV, wifi, parking
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Hire the caterer and confirm dietary and allergy options

    Ask for a vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free count on the RSVP.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Arrange AV: sound, microphones, projector, and screens

    Always schedule a tech check the day before or morning of.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Book speakers, entertainment, or a host, and confirm their needs
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Build the run-of-show: a minute-by-minute timeline for the day
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Send invitations or open registration, and track RSVPs
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Plan decor, signage, and any branding or printed materials
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Sort transportation, directions, and parking for attendees
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Confirm permits, licenses, and event insurance

    Alcohol, amplified music, and public spaces often need permits.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Line up staff or volunteers and give each a clear role
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Prepare a day-of contact sheet with every vendor and lead's number
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Plan cleanup, teardown, and who returns rentals
  • check_box_outline_blank
    After the event: send thank-yous and gather feedback while it's fresh

Frequently asked questions

How do I start planning an event? expand_more

Start with the goal and the budget — everything else flows from those two. Once you know what success looks like and what you can spend, set the date, book the venue, and confirm your headcount. From there you can layer in catering, AV, and the run-of-show.

What is a run-of-show? expand_more

A run-of-show is a minute-by-minute timeline of the event: when doors open, when each speaker or activity starts, cue points for AV, and when things wrap. It keeps staff, vendors, and hosts in sync so no one has to improvise on the day.

How far ahead should I plan an event? expand_more

For a small event, 6 to 8 weeks is usually enough. For a large conference or gala, start 4 to 6 months out so you can secure the venue, speakers, and catering. Book the venue and any keynote speakers first, since they have the least flexibility.
